reason: Alert 1 (java/ssrf): alert-TP — User input 'param' is assigned to 'host' at line 38 ('String host = param;'). While a check at line 39 ('if (isNonPublicAddress(resolveHost(host))) return;') attempts to block certain internal addresses, it relies on standard Java InetAddress methods which may not cover all private IPv4 ranges (e.g., 10.0.0.0/8) effectively, and critically, it permits connections to any external public domain. Since the sink at line 43 ('new java.net.URL("http://" + host + "/v1").openConnection();') uses the unresolved 'host' variable, an attacker can supply a public hostname to trigger an SSRF attack. The resolved sink value depends on attacker-controlled input.

evidence.note: Outbound connection made using 'host' variable containing user input
